name: CUMIPMT
description: CUMIPMT returns the total interest paid over a specified range of periods for a loan with constant payments and a constant interest rate.
tldr: Calculates the cumulative interest paid on a loan between two periods.

parameters.name: start_period
parameters.description: First period in the range to include.

parameters.name: end_period
parameters.description: Last period in the range to include.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: 0 = end of period, 1 = beginning of period.

basicExample.description: Total interest paid in the first year of a loan
basicExample.explanation: For a $300,000 mortgage at 5% over 30 years, the first year of interest is about $14,935.

advancedExamples.title: Cumulative interest over several years
advancedExamples.description: Interest paid in years 6-10 of a mortgage
advancedExamples.explanation: Calculates interest paid during the 61st through 120th monthly payments.

howItWorks: CUMIPMT sums the interest portions of all payments from start_period to end_period. It uses the same amortization logic as PMT and IPMT.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: The type argument is required, not optional.
Returns a negative value because interest is an outflow.

commonErrors.cause: start_period or end_period is invalid, or type is not 0 or 1.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure 1 <= start_period <= end_period <= nper and type is 0 or 1.

commonErrors.cause: Annual rate was not divided by 12.
commonErrors.fix: Use the monthly rate for monthly periods.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: CUMIPMT works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between CUMIPMT and IPMT?
faq.answer: IPMT returns interest for one period. CUMIPMT returns interest summed over a range of periods.

faq.question: Can CUMIPMT be used for taxes?
faq.answer: Yes, mortgage interest is often tax-deductible, and CUMIPMT can help estimate annual interest.

faq.question: Why is CUMIPMT negative?
faq.answer: It represents interest paid out. Use -CUMIPMT or ABS for a positive value.
